text:
jin: Quick heads-up — I finished the FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff across summarization, retrieval-augmented generation, and codegen. AWQ shows best latency but we’re seeing a measurable hallucination spike on the summarization suite.
sara: how big is "measurable"? numbers? :eyes:
jin: Baseline is fp32 -> GPTQ -> INT8 -> AWQ -> FP8 ordering for cost/latency. Short excerpt of metrics (summary set A, 1k samples):
jin: ```
Model     | ROUGE-L | Hallucination rate | Code-format errors | Median p50 latency
fp32      | 0.72    | 0.012              | 0.003               | 320ms
GPTQ-4bit | 0.71    | 0.013              | 0.004               | 180ms
INT8      | 0.70    | 0.015              | 0.006               | 140ms
AWQ       | 0.69    | 0.028  <-- spike   | 0.010               | 95ms
FP8       | 0.69    | 0.018              | 0.008               | 110ms
```
jin: Hallucination rate = fraction of samples with unsupported facts added (human-eval). AWQ is ~2.8x baseline on this set.
michael: that's pretty big. is it concentrated on a few prompt templates or across the board?
jin: concentrated. templates that rely on temporal grounding and multi-sentence factual compression (news -> concise timeline) are worst. Codegen regressions are smaller but visible: mismatched closing parens, stray backticks in inline code.
sara: can you paste one of the failing summarization examples (input, gold, awq output)?
jin: sure — example below. note this is fairly short.
jin: INPUT: "Summarize: Mayor announced the new climate fund on March 3, 2023, then held town halls in April."
jin: GOLD: "Mayor launched a climate fund on March 3, 2023, followed by town halls in April."
jin: AWQ OUTPUT: "Mayor launched a climate fund on March 3, 2024, followed by town halls in April. He promised to fund new coastal projects." <-- added year change + invented project
thomas: interesting — the year flip looks like a numeric token misalignment/scale issue rather than hallucination from content mixing. Could be quantization scaling for number tokens.
michael: did you check tokenizer/decoding differences? AWQ runtime might be using an alternate token rounding for logits.
jin: I double-checked decoding kwargs (same top_p/temperature/forced-bos). Tokenization identical. My suspicion: AWQ quantization mapping combined with prefix KV cache truncation causes small bias on number tokens so sampling drifts.
sara: any repro in deterministic argmax sampling? if argmax flips year then it's not sampling randomness.
jin: ran argmax (greedy) — AWQ still chooses 2024 in 18/200 fails. So it's deterministic shift for those tokens.
michael: can you run a per-token logit comparison for the year token across fp32 vs awq for that example? even a small offset could cascade.
jin: planning that next. quick logit diff I pulled for token ids around "2023" / "2024":
jin: ```
Token   fp32_logit   awq_logit   diff
"2023"  -1.2          -2.1       -0.9
"2024"  -1.6          -1.3       +0.3
```
jin: awq lowers logits for 2023 and raises 2024, so argmax flips.
thomas: that supports quant scaling issue. could be per-channel calibration or per-head outliers. Did you try post-quant calibration with a small calibration set?
jin: ran a 1k-sample linear bias correction on final layer logits — hallucination rate for AWQ drops to 0.017 (closer to FP8). latency unchanged.
sara: nice. was quality fully recovered on codegen formatting errors too?
jin: partial. formatting errors reduced by 40% after calibration, but some structural tokenization artifacts persist in deeper sequences.
michael: what's the rollout plan? we can't ship AWQ as default for summaries yet.
sara: suggest routing policy: use AWQ for low-risk text-gen (chatty assistants) and pin summarization endpoints to GPTQ or calibrated-AWQ until we have a robust correction.
jin: agreed. I'll prepare per-route eval: run the summarization regression harness (5k examples) and produce a calibrated-AWQ build + per-token calibration table.
eval-bot: Scheduled per-route eval: summarization-harness-5k at 2026-03-18T17:05Z. ETA 45m.
michael: also file an infra ticket to add per-head quant debug dumps so we can trace whether a specific attention head is the culprit.
thomas: will take that on. I'll also try AWQ re-quant with per-channel clip instead of global.
sara: action items: jin -> run 5k eval + logit diffs; thomas -> re-quant experiments; michael -> infra dump ticket; sara -> prepare rollout pin + customer comm draft if needed. :white_check_mark:
jin: I'll post the 5k results thread when eval-bot finishes. thanks all.
